verdicts.strongest_argument: The arithmetic is CORRECT — I checked every term against the primary releases. Q1 FY26 adj EBITDA $17.6M, Q2 $22.2M, Q3 $30.495M = $70.295M against a raised $85-90M guide, so implied Q4 is $14.7-19.7M; 9M revenue $236.1+$239.7+$251.943 = $727.7M against $950-975M, so implied Q4 revenue is $222.3-247.3M, a sequential decline from $251.9M and a 4.1-5.5pp margin step-down. The FY2025 analog is also exactly right: 9M FY25 adj EBITDA $23.1M against a reaffirmed $24-31M guide (implied Q4 $0.9-7.9M), actual Q4 $11.3M, FY $34.5M = 11.3% above the top. So no refutation on the sums. What kills most of the edge is that the Street has already done this subtraction and already assumes the beat: consensus Q4 FY26 revenue is $238.2-243.0M (above the $234.8M implied midpoint) and consensus EPS $0.07, with KeyBanc at $0.09 — on this company's ~$10M/qtr EBITDA-to-net-income bridge that puts consensus adj EBITDA at roughly $19.5M, i.e. AT the top of the implied guidance range, and KeyBanc above it. The 'guidance is sandbagged' observation is therefore embedded, not new. Worse for the mechanism, the identical setup exactly one year ago — the 2025-09-09 print, where Q4 FY25 came in at $11.3M versus an implied $0.9-7.9M and the full year landed 11% above the top of guidance — produced a reaction of only -2.81%, because the initial forward-year guide dominated. The baseline's own reaction history is the argument against this finding paying.

prior_publication.what_it_says: The Q3 FY2026 release itself publishes the $30.495M quarterly adj EBITDA, the $251.943M revenue and the raised $950-975M / $85-90M full-year guide — every input to the claim's arithmetic.

Today's preview states consensus Q4 FY26 revenue of $238.22M — a sequential decline from $251.94M — and EPS of $0.0675, showing the sequential revenue fall the claim treats as implausible is in fact the published consensus.
KeyCorp raised its Q4 FY2026 EPS estimate to $0.09 from $0.07 with an Overweight and $13 target, i.e. a sell-side model already sitting above the top of the guidance-implied Q4.
Confirms the FY2025 analog terms: 9M adj EBITDA $23.1M and reaffirmed FY25 guidance of $815-865M revenue / $24-31M adj EBITDA.
Confirms Q4 FY25 adj EBITDA of $11.3M and FY25 of $34.5M — the beat the claim cites — on the print that moved the stock only -2.81%.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: The single most relevant prior reaction is 2025-09-09 (-2.81%), the same fiscal-Q4-plus-first-forward-guide event in which exactly this guidance-implied-Q4 beat occurred and was almost entirely ignored. By contrast the two large reactions in the history — 2026-02-03 (+37.46%) and 2025-11-04 (-17.56%) — were guidance-revision quarters, not Q4/full-year prints. Spot 10.25 with a 20-day run-up of -5.96% is not a tape that has been bid up in anticipation of a blowout Q4, which is the one point in the finding's favour.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: A published Q4 adjusted EBITDA consensus materially BELOW $19.7M (i.e. the Street taking the implied guide literally rather than looking through it) would take this to the 25-35 range.

verdicts.strongest_argument: The direction of this claim is management's own published guidance commentary from four months ago and it made a wire headline the same day: on the 2026-05-05 call the CFO said 'initial indications suggest rate increases in fiscal 2027 may be lower than what we have experienced historically', management flagged 'rate pressures emerge as we engage with our state Medicaid partners', and Seeking Alpha's news item was literally titled '...for fiscal 2026 amid early 2027 rate pressure signals'. The Colorado specifics are also public, and the largest of them is a year old, not new: the reset of most FFS rates to 85% of Medicare effective 2026-04-01 was published in HCPF's Special Provider Bulletin on rate reductions (B2500528) in September 2025 and was already in effect before the May call. The $270M and the 2% across-the-board cut effective 2026-07-01 came out of the Long Bill Polis signed on 2026-05-08 and were covered that week by CPR and roughly eight Colorado newspapers. So the finding's framing — 'published in the June 2026 provider bulletin after InnovAge last spoke to investors' — is right for the 2% HCBS piece and materially wrong for the 85%-of-Medicare piece, which is the bigger number. What I could NOT find published anywhere is the specific step the finding takes: PACE capitation set beneath a UPL derived from those same FFS/HCBS costs, therefore InnovAge's FY2027 Colorado rate flat-to-down. No sell-side note, no trade piece, and no company statement makes that link or sizes it, and HCPF's own FY2026-27 MSP budget request actually anticipates PACE expenditure GROWTH on enrollment, which cuts the other way. That unpublished linkage plus the fact that tonight is the first FY2027 guide is why this is not above 65.

prior_publication.what_it_says: Management said FY2027 Medicaid rate increases 'may be lower than what we have experienced historically', cited post-pandemic funding and state budget pressures, and guided Medicare PACE rates to only 1.5-2.0% in FY2027.
Headline itself frames the quarter as raised FY26 guidance 'amid early 2027 rate pressure signals' — the theme was in the wire copy on the day.

Polis signed the $46.8bn FY2026-27 budget on 2026-05-08 with a 2% cut to reimbursement rates for most Medicaid providers and roughly $270M of benefit and provider-rate savings — the finding's headline number, in general-interest press, four months ago.
HCPF's September 2025 special bulletin on rate reductions is where the reduction of most FFS rates to 85% of Medicare from 2026-04-01 was first published — a year before this finding dates it.

The cited June bulletin confirms the 2.0% across-the-board reduction on HCBS waiver services for dates of service on or after 2026-07-01, needing no CMS approval — implementation detail on a cut already legislated on 2026-05-08.

Trade coverage of InnovAge specifically lobbying against Medicaid cut threats — the company-level exposure to Medicaid cuts is an established trade-press theme, though this piece does not size Colorado.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: The tape is consistent with partial pricing and nothing stronger: the 52-week high of $12.64 was set 2026-06-30 and the stock has bled to 10.25 (-5.09% 5d, -5.96% 20d), so roughly a fifth has come off since the June bulletin period, though the 2026-08-04 sponsor-registration drop accounts for about 6pp of that on its own. The relevant precedent for a guide-driven disappointment is 2025-11-04, -17.56%. There is no option chain (15 contracts total open interest), so no skew and no implied move can be cited either way.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: A published sell-side note or trade piece between June and today that quantifies Colorado PACE capitation as flat-to-down for InnovAge's FY2027 would push this to 80; conversely, evidence that Colorado exempted PACE capitation from the 2% ATB and held the PACE UPL harmless would make it factually wrong rather than priced.

verdicts.strongest_argument: The registration is not obscure and it visibly moved the price. The S-3 hit EDGAR at 16:11 on Friday 2026-07-31; the stock fell 5.79% on Tuesday 2026-08-04, the second trading day after, and the effectiveness notice followed on 2026-08-05. It was written up by MarketScreener ('InnovAge Registers 113 Million Shares for Potential Resale by TCO Group Holdings'), StockTitan ('InnovAge holders register 113M shares for resale'), and twice by Simply Wall St, syndicated to Webull — all of which name TCO Group Holdings, the 112,988,070 shares, the 83.2% stake, the Apax and Welsh Carson vehicles, and explicitly the 'sizable potential secondary overhang'. So the finding's own framing that this happened 'with no 8-K and no press release at any point' is technically true of company disclosure and misleading about what the market saw. The Rule 144 arithmetic is right — 1% of 135,736,393 is 1.357M and beats the 878k average weekly volume test — and I do not dispute that removing the cap matters. What is genuinely unpublished is only the timing inference: that the print plus a Wells Fargo Healthcare Conference slot at 08:00 ET on 2026-09-09 is the sequencing for a marketed block. That is a plausible read but it is speculation stacked on a published fact, and the same schedule is the ordinary way a company times a fiscal-year print, so it does not carry the finding on its own. It also mostly resolves after the earnings reaction window rather than inside it.

prior_publication.what_it_says: Headline coverage of the resale registration of 112,988,070 shares by TCO Group Holdings.
Filing summary dated to the 16:11 EDGAR acceptance, naming the 83.2% stake and flagging a 'sizable potential secondary overhang if holders elect to sell'.
Retail-facing article on what the US$1.31bn resale registration means for shareholders, naming Apax and Welsh Carson.
Coverage of the EFFECT notice on 2026-08-05, i.e. the shelf going effective was itself reported.
Notes shares falling 6.4% to $10.23 in the aftermath of the registration, without attributing a cause — corroborating that the de-rating happened in early-to-mid August.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: This is the one finding with a clean price print against it: -5.79% on 2026-08-04, immediately after the 2026-07-31 post-close filing, and the 52-week high of $12.64 dated 2026-06-30 has not been revisited since. Spot 10.25 sits about 15% below that high with a -5.96% 20-day run-up, which is what a live sponsor overhang into a print looks like. No skew is available to confirm it (front expiry has 15 contracts of open interest, put/call OI ratio 0.07), so the tape is the only witness — but here the tape is enough.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: Evidence that the prior IPO-era resale registration had NOT lapsed — making this pure housekeeping rather than a new capability — would lower my size to about -0.5; an actual filed prospectus supplement or underwriter mandate would raise the size but not lower the priced-in number.

interactions: INNV#0 and INNV#1 rest on the same two documents — the 2026-05-05 earnings release and its call transcript — and they point opposite ways on the same print, which is the central interaction here. Both can be true at once, and in fact were true simultaneously on 2025-09-09: Q4 FY25 adjusted EBITDA of $11.3M crushed the $0.9-7.9M implied by guidance and the full year finished 11% above the top, yet the stock fell 2.81% because the initial FY26 guide of $56-65M was the number that mattered. That precedent argues the Q4 beat in #0 is close to a free option with no payoff and that the FY2027 guide carrying #1's Colorado exposure is what tonight is actually about, so the two should not be netted as equal-weight opposites. Second interaction, cutting against #1's sign: if #2 is right that Apax and Welsh Carson intend to market a block in the window after this print, the sponsors' interest is a supportive FY2027 guide, not a conservative one — the same incentive that #0 relies on for the sandbag to unwind now argues the FY2027 guide is set to look good rather than to be de-risked. Finally, #1's 'after InnovAge last spoke to investors' premise splits: the 2% HCBS cut genuinely post-dates the 2026-05-05 call (budget signed 2026-05-08), but the 85%-of-Medicare FFS reset it bundles in was published in HCPF's September 2025 bulletin and was already in effect on 2026-04-01, so the two components of that single finding have very different novelty and should not be credited at one rate.
